messages.subject: Calverton / Ferncliffe - response to LBA
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Sirs,

We act for Ferncliffe Alloys Limited. Please find our response to your letter before action attached. In short, liability is denied; our client relied on the mill certification and wishes to inspect the retained material before matters go further. We are willing in principle to discuss ADR once the technical documents have been exchanged.

Yours faithfully
Oliver Jennings
Birchall Stone LLP

messages.subject: Ferncliffe response - summary and recommendation
messages.plaintextBody:
Patricia,

Ferncliffe (via Birchall Stone) have denied liability. Their main points are: (1) they relied on the mill certificate as a stockholder; (2) they have not yet seen the full Wraysbury report or inspected the material; and (3) the failures may be down to our machining/installation. None of this surprises us.

My recommendation is that we (a) offer the retained bar and assemblies for joint inspection, (b) consider issuing proceedings to keep up the pressure, and (c) instruct counsel for a merits and quantum advice before we commit to litigation. I'll get a draft letter to them and speak to Harriet Stanford's clerks about the advice.

The stockholder defence does not help them as against us - they sold us the bar, so they are responsible for it regardless of where they got it.

Tom Gallagher
Associate, Dispute Resolution
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0148

Confidential and may be legally privileged.
